Among the candidates with internally comparable evaluation context, the Cancer PRSweb GWAS-hits siblings provide the strongest visible discrimination/effect-size evidence: PGS000611 (GWAS Hits, 13 variants; UKB-trained) shows AUROC 0.567 with relatively high Nagelkerke R² 0.0114 and a notably stronger top-1%-vs-rest OR 2.66 (1.79–3.93) than other nearby options (e.g., PGS000610/612 and PGS000613). This makes PGS000611 the best-supported choice from the available metadata, but confidence is limited because the key metrics are still full-model and covariate sets differ across publications (and some high AUROCs in other models likely reflect additional covariates such as smoking/BMI), preventing a clean PRS-only comparison.

All 20 candidates are direct matches for urinary bladder cancer (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported consistently indicate bladder cancer/cancer of bladder/urothelial carcinoma). No candidate reports PRS-only AUROC/R2, so full-model AUROC values are not directly comparable as PRS discrimination; selection must lean on endpoint fidelity plus method/structural evidence and available effect sizes. Among the PRSweb bladder cancer siblings with highly comparable endpoints/covariates, PGS000611 (GWAS Hits; 13 variants; UKB-based) shows the strongest available risk-stratification signal (OR top 1% vs rest = 2.66, 95% CI 1.79–3.93) with similar per-SD OR (~1.28) and similar full-model AUROC (~0.567) to its close peers, making it the best-supported choice within that coherent cluster. Main limitation: evidence remains sub-optimal because metrics are largely full-model (covariate-influenced) and several near-equivalent direct-match candidates exist (e.g., PGS000610/PGS000612, PGS000613 with similar AUROC/OR but different training size), so the superiority of PGS000611 cannot be established with high certainty from the visible metadata alone.

All 20 candidates are direct matches for urinary bladder cancer (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported consistently refer to bladder cancer/urinary bladder carcinoma). However, most models lack PRS-only (covariates-regressed-out) discrimination metrics; several report only full-model AUROC, which domain guidance says is not comparable to PRS performance, especially when covariates include age/smoking/BMI (e.g., PGS000071, PGS000782). Within the large coherent PRSweb bladder-cancer cluster (PGS000607–PGS000616), the GWAS-hits family shows the strongest reported per-SD effect sizes (OR≈1.28–1.29) and has materially better full-model AUROC (~0.567) than the PRS-CS/lassosum siblings (~0.52–0.54). Between the two top GWAS-hits siblings, PGS000611 is preferred over PGS000610 due to stronger extreme-risk separation (top 1% vs rest OR=2.66 vs 1.47) and similar per-SD OR, with consistent endpoint/covariates. Limitation: the selected evidence is still based on full-model AUROC plus effect sizes rather than PRS-only AUC/R2, and cross-study comparisons (e.g., vs PGS000723/PGS004687/PGS004241) remain uncertain due to metric incomparability and missing covariate details in some records.

All 19 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with generally aligned phenotyping_reported (Angina / ICD10 I20 / PheCode 411.3). Among models with clearly PRS-comparable metrics, PGS001262 reports the strongest PGS-only discrimination (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.58683; PGS R² (no covariates)=0.01304) and the largest incremental AUROC (0.0098) while using only basic covariates (age, sex, array type, genotype PCs). Competing snpnet siblings PGS001260 and PGS001261 have slightly weaker PGS-only AUROC/R² and similar covariates; PGS000703 lacks PRS-only metrics (only full-model AUROC=0.5926) and uses a multi-PRS label but without PRS-comparable performance evidence here. Newer UKB I20 models (PGS004457/PGS004527) report only ORs with unknown covariates (no AUC/R²), and the MVP portability-method comparison set (PGS005047–PGS005059) provides only full-model C-index plus ORs, which are not directly comparable to PRS-only performance. Main limitation: evidence is still UKB-centric for the preferred model and non-European validation performance is not shown despite a multi-ancestry eval distribution, so external transportability beyond European validation remains uncertain.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping strings are aligned: Angina/I20/PheCode 411.3). Among models with comparable PRS-oriented signals, PGS005052 reports one of the strongest per-SD effect sizes (OR=1.491, 95% CI 1.42–1.57) and also has high reported discrimination (C-index=0.766) with basic covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), which is supportive. However, confidence is low and the overall outcome is sub-optimal because (i) for the MVP-derived 2024 set (PGS005048/005050/005051/005052/005057/005058 and related), several near-clone candidates show essentially indistinguishable C-index values (~0.764–0.766) and very similar ORs (~1.45–1.49), making it hard to identify a uniquely best model from the visible metadata alone; and (ii) other direct-match options either lack PRS-comparable metrics entirely (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527) or are from a known pan-trait sparse framework (PGS001260–PGS001262) where full-model AUROC is likely covariate-driven despite reported incremental metrics. Given the close competition within the MVP cluster and incomplete comparability across studies, a single clearly best-supported direct-match model cannot be selected with high certainty.

All 19 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with broadly aligned phenotyping (Angina / ICD10 I20 / PheCode 411.3), so selection hinges on method/performance evidence. PGS005052 (angina pectoris PheCode 411.3; ldpred; 1,286,612 variants; MVP-trained with multi-ancestry eval) has strong structural support (genome-wide shrinkage with very high variant count) and is among the top reported European validation discrimination values in this set (full-model C-index 0.7662) with a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.491). Competing models include the UKB snpnet sparse pan-trait family (PGS001260/1261/1262), which reports explicit PRS-only metrics but has much smaller variant counts (~1.8k–2.6k) and modest PRS-only AUC (~0.58), and the Commun Biol I20 models (PGS004457/PGS004527) which provide only ORs and have unknown covariates/limited comparable metrics. The main limitation is that for the MVP ldpred/prscs family the reported C-index is a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² shown here), making cross-model comparability imperfect; therefore the choice is supported but not definitive.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo matches; phenotyping_reported is angina/ICD10 I20/phecode 411.3 variants). Among models with clearly PRS-comparable metrics, the PLoS Genet snpnet family (PGS001260/61/62) reports PGS-only AUROC (~0.58–0.59) and PGS R2 (~0.012–0.013) plus incremental AUROC, allowing interpretation beyond covariate-driven full-model AUROC. PGS001262 is preferred within that family because it uses a direct doctor-diagnosed angina endpoint and has the strongest full-model AUROC (0.807) and highest PGS R2 (0.01304) of the three while keeping covariates to basic demographics/PCs/array. Limitation: several newer genome-wide shrinkage scores (e.g., LDpred2 / PRS-CS / PRS-CSx; PGS004457/PGS0050xx) have more favorable method/variant-count properties and sometimes strong per-SD ORs, but most lack explicit PRS-only AUC/R2 in the provided metadata, making cross-model ranking uncertain; thus the selection is supportable but not high-certainty.

All 19 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with largely UKB/MVP-derived endpoints. Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, PGS001262 has endpoint-fidelity consistent with the target (phenotyping_reported: doctor-diagnosed angina) and provides explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.58683; PGS R2 no covariates=0.01304) plus incremental AUROC (0.0098), which is more informative than models reporting only full-model metrics or only an OR without discrimination. Competing snpnet siblings PGS001260/PGS001261 have similar PRS-only metrics but slightly weaker than PGS001262, while PGS000703 reports only a full-model AUROC (not PRS-comparable) and the 2024 Commun Biol scores (PGS004457/PGS004527) report only ORs with unknown covariates. All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris by trait_efo, with several closely related endpoint instantiations. PGS001262 has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: doctor-diagnosed angina), uses basic covariates (age, sex, array type, PCs), and provides PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.58683) and PGS R2 (no covariates) (0.01304), which are interpretable and below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0092; h2_liability=0.1337) on at least the liability scale. Although its full-model AUROC is high (0.80729), the incremental AUROC is small (0.0098), indicating much of the full-model discrimination is covariate-driven rather than PRS-driven, consistent with domain guidance. Competing candidates remain meaningful: PGS001261 (time-to-event angina pectoris) has slightly higher PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.58233; PGS R2 0.01228) and higher full-model AUROC (0.74852) but differs by time-to-event endpoint; newer UKB/MVP models (e.g., PGS005052/PGS005057) report strong effect sizes and C-index but lack clearly PRS-only performance and have mixed multi-ancestry evaluation context, limiting direct comparability. Because multiple endpoint-faithful models are close and metric comparability is imperfect across families, the selection is supported but not definitive.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (EFO alignment and phenotyping_reported includes Angina/I20/PheCode 411.3 variants). However, confidence is lowered because the key discrimination metric is a full-model C-index (not explicitly PRS-only), samples_training is listed as N/A, and several sibling models in the same publication have near-identical C-index/OR (making the ‘best’ choice only marginally supported). UKB snpnet models (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) do report explicit PGS-only AUROC/R², but are from a known pan-trait sparse framework and show modest PRS-only signal, while the 2024 Commun Biol scores (PGS004457/PGS004527) report only ORs with unknown covariates and no comparable PRS-only metrics, so they do not clearly outrank the MVP cluster based on the visible evidence.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris by trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping strings (e.g., ICD10 I20, PheCode 411.3, or angina). Multiple direct-match candidates exist with coherent endpoint alignment to squamous cell carcinoma (e.g., PGS000120, PGS000460–PGS000468, PGS000731, PGS005209). Among these, PGS000461 has the strongest visible discrimination/effect-size evidence within the largest coherent same-endpoint cluster (Cancer PRSweb, Am J Hum Genet 2020): full-model AUROC 0.599 (0.579–0.618), Nagelkerke R² 0.0304, and OR per SD 1.491 (1.395–1.593), with only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4). It also shows a strong tail effect (top 1% vs rest OR 3.51). Key limitation: across candidates, the reported AUROCs are full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), so residual uncertainty remains about standalone PRS contribution; hence confidence is Moderate rather than High.

Direct-match candidates for the target concept (uterine cancer) are present: PGS001795 (phenotyping_reported: “Uterine cancer”), PGS000541/PGS000542 (phenotyping_reported: “Malignant neoplasm of uterus”, trait_efo: “uterine cancer”), and PGS003740 (trait_reported: “Corpus Uteri”, uterine corpus cancer). Key limitation: the available performance evidence for uterine cancer is limited and mostly not PRS-only comparable (e.g., AUROC=0.66 is a full-model metric; the only PRS-comparable metric shown is a small pgs_only_r2=0.001948), and there is meaningful competition from other direct uterine-cancer-coded models (PGS000541/PGS000542) with reported ORs/top-1% ORs but weaker method structure.
